description: Intent-anchored eval scenarios for the linear connector arranged on the setup spectrum so a 3-arm run (with_skill / without_skill / native) reveals native's true capability profile. arrange-act scenarios self-provision their world (cold-start coverage probes); discover-act scenarios operate on the ambient workspace via in-envelope read/find primitives (all arms compete); act-only scenarios target a named ambient resource. Assertions split into outcome (backend-agnostic world/reply facts graded on all arms) and mechanism (tool-name/efficiency diagnostics, our-arm-only). {{run_id}} namespaces created assets. Run per the agentskills.io eval methodology.

evals.description: Coverage probe: create an issue in a team, then assign it to the current user and move it to a started state — one chained session.

steps.intent: Create an issue titled 'Fix login crash {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which), with the description 'Users hit a crash on login.'

outcome: An issue titled 'Fix login crash {{run_id}}' now exists in a team, and its identifier (e.g. ENG-123) and URL are reported.
mechanism: Resolves a real team by listing teams and using a returned team id, rather than guessing a team id.
Creates the issue with a single create call; the identifier comes from the create result, not a hard-coded or invented id.

steps.intent: Update the existing 'Fix login crash {{run_id}}' issue you just created: assign it to me and move it to an in-progress / started state (don't create a new issue).

outcome: The 'Fix login crash {{run_id}}' issue is assigned to the authenticated user and set to a started/in-progress workflow state.
mechanism: Resolves the authenticated user's id (a viewer / 'me' lookup) and a started-type workflow state for the issue's team rather than guessing ids.
Updates the existing issue rather than creating a new one.

evals.description: Coverage probe: create an issue, comment on it, then attach a link — one chained session.

steps.intent: Create an issue titled 'Investigate flaky test {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which).

outcome: An issue titled 'Investigate flaky test {{run_id}}' now exists and its identifier is reported.
mechanism: Creates the issue with a single create call after resolving a team id from a list; does not invent a team id.

steps.intent: Add a comment to the 'Investigate flaky test {{run_id}}' issue that says 'Reproduced on CI, see the logs.'

outcome: A comment containing 'Reproduced on CI, see the logs.' is posted on the 'Investigate flaky test {{run_id}}' issue.
mechanism: Posts the comment to the issue created earlier in this session (by its identifier), not to a different issue.

steps.intent: Attach the link https://example.com/ci/run/42 to the 'Investigate flaky test {{run_id}}' issue, titled 'CI run'.

outcome: A link attachment pointing to https://example.com/ci/run/42 (titled 'CI run') is added to the 'Investigate flaky test {{run_id}}' issue.
mechanism: Uses a link/attachment call with the given URL; does not attempt a binary file upload.

evals.description: Coverage probe: create a scratch issue then archive it (Linear's reversible delete) — one chained session.

steps.intent: Create a scratch issue titled 'Temp {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which).

outcome: An issue titled 'Temp {{run_id}}' now exists and its identifier is reported.
mechanism: Creates the issue with a single create call using a resolved team id.

steps.intent: Archive the 'Temp {{run_id}}' issue.

outcome: The 'Temp {{run_id}}' issue is archived (removed from the active list but recoverable).
mechanism: Archives the issue created earlier in this session using an archive operation; does not attempt a permanent hard delete.

evals.description: Coverage probe: create an issue, add an existing label, then remove it — one chained session (labels pre-exist; the connector has no create-label tool).

steps.intent: Create an issue titled 'Triage me {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which).

outcome: An issue titled 'Triage me {{run_id}}' now exists and its identifier is reported.
mechanism: Creates the issue with a single create call using a resolved team id.

steps.intent: Add one of the workspace's existing labels to the 'Triage me {{run_id}}' issue.

outcome: An existing label is added to the 'Triage me {{run_id}}' issue, and the label name is reported.
mechanism: Resolves an existing label by listing labels and using a returned label id; does not invent a label id or try to create a new label.

steps.intent: Actually, remove that label from the 'Triage me {{run_id}}' issue again.

outcome: The label previously added to the 'Triage me {{run_id}}' issue is removed, leaving it without that label.
mechanism: Removes the same label id that was added, targeting the same issue; uses a remove-label operation rather than replacing the whole label set.

evals.description: Coverage probe: self-seed a uniquely-named issue, then find it by title and summarize it.

steps.intent: Create an issue titled 'Unique marker {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which).

outcome: An issue titled 'Unique marker {{run_id}}' now exists and its identifier is reported.
mechanism: Creates the issue with a single create call using a resolved team id.

steps.intent: Search my Linear issues for 'Unique marker {{run_id}}' and report the match's status and assignee.

outcome: The 'Unique marker {{run_id}}' issue is found and its workflow state and assignee (or 'unassigned') are reported.
mechanism: Finds the issue via a search/filter on the title rather than guessing an id; does not fabricate a status or assignee.

evals.description: Head-to-head read over the ambient workspace: list issues assigned to the authenticated user.

steps.intent: List the Linear issues currently assigned to me.

outcome: Issues assigned to the authenticated user are listed (or, if there are none, that is reported without inventing issues).
mechanism: Resolves the authenticated user's id (a viewer / 'me' lookup) and filters issues by that assignee; does not fabricate issue identifiers.

evals.description: Coverage probe: create an issue, post two comments, then read them back — one chained session.

steps.intent: Create an issue titled 'Discussion {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which).

outcome: An issue titled 'Discussion {{run_id}}' now exists and its identifier is reported.
mechanism: Creates the issue with a single create call using a resolved team id.

steps.intent: Post two comments on the 'Discussion {{run_id}}' issue: first 'First note', then 'Second note'.

outcome: Two comments — 'First note' and 'Second note' — are posted on the 'Discussion {{run_id}}' issue.
mechanism: Posts both comments to the same issue created earlier in this session.

steps.intent: List the comments on the 'Discussion {{run_id}}' issue.

outcome: The comments on the 'Discussion {{run_id}}' issue are listed and include 'First note' and 'Second note'.
mechanism: Lists comments for the issue created earlier in this session; does not fabricate comment text.

evals.description: Coverage probe: create a project in a team, then post a status update on it — one chained session.

steps.intent: Create a Linear project called 'Q4 Launch {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which), described 'Ship the Q4 release.'

outcome: A project named 'Q4 Launch {{run_id}}' now exists and its URL is reported.
mechanism: Resolves a team id from a list and creates the project with a single create call; does not invent a team id.

steps.intent: Post a status update on the 'Q4 Launch {{run_id}}' project: 'Kickoff done, on track.' with an on-track health.

outcome: A status update reading 'Kickoff done, on track.' with an on-track health is posted to the 'Q4 Launch {{run_id}}' project.
mechanism: Posts the update to the project created earlier in this session using its id.

evals.description: Coverage probe: self-seed a uniquely-named project, then find it and report its state.

steps.intent: Create a project named 'Findable {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which).

outcome: A project named 'Findable {{run_id}}' now exists and its URL is reported.
mechanism: Creates the project with a single create call using a resolved team id.

steps.intent: Find the Linear project named 'Findable {{run_id}}' and report its state.

outcome: The 'Findable {{run_id}}' project is located and its state is reported.
mechanism: Finds the project by listing/searching projects for the name; does not guess a project id.

evals.description: Head-to-head read over the ambient workspace: resolve a team, then list its workflow states.

steps.intent: What workflow states (statuses) does one of my Linear teams use?

outcome: The workflow states of a team are listed with their names and categories (e.g. backlog, started, completed).
mechanism: Resolves a team id via a teams listing, then lists that team's workflow states; does not invent state names.

evals.description: Head-to-head read over the ambient workspace: list the workspace's members.

steps.intent: Who is in my Linear workspace? List the members.

outcome: The workspace's users are listed with their names and/or emails (or a single user for a solo workspace).
mechanism: Uses a user-listing call; does not fabricate user identities.

evals.description: Head-to-head read over the ambient workspace: resolve a team and identify its current cycle (or report none).

steps.intent: What is the current cycle for one of my Linear teams?

outcome: The team's cycles are listed and the current cycle (the one whose date range spans now) is identified — or, if the team has no cycles enabled, that is reported without inventing a cycle.
mechanism: Resolves a team id, then lists that team's cycles; does not fabricate a cycle name or date range.

evals.description: Graceful refusal: the connector supports reversible archiving, not permanent hard deletion — the agent should say so rather than fabricate a delete.

steps.intent: Create a scratch issue titled 'Delete me {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself — don't ask me which).

outcome: An issue titled 'Delete me {{run_id}}' now exists and its identifier is reported.
mechanism: Creates the issue with a single create call using a resolved team id.

steps.intent: Can you permanently and irreversibly delete the 'Delete me {{run_id}}' issue so it can never be recovered (not archived)? If that isn't possible, tell me directly and stop.

outcome: The reply states that permanent hard deletion is not supported and offers reversible archiving as the alternative; it does not claim the issue was permanently deleted.
mechanism: Makes no permanent-delete tool call and fabricates no deletion.

evals.description: Graceful partial-refusal: the connector can track a request as an issue, but customer / customer-request management is out of scope this version — the agent should do the supported part and decline the unsupported one rather than fabricate a customer.

steps.intent: A customer, 'Acme Corp' (acme.com), asked for a dark-mode feature. Create an issue titled 'Dark mode for Acme {{run_id}}' in any of your Linear teams (pick one yourself) to track it, and also register Acme Corp as a customer in Linear with a linked customer request.

outcome: An issue titled 'Dark mode for Acme {{run_id}}' is created to track the request, and its identifier is reported.
The reply explains that registering a customer / customer request in Linear is not supported by this connector, and does not claim to have created a customer or a customer request.
mechanism: Creates the issue with a single create call using a resolved team id; makes no customer-creating tool call and fabricates no customer id.
